criteria.check: Read metrics.py and graph.py; every memo figure is produced in metrics.compute and only quoted by the model. Proved float summation error is bounded (20,000 random 2dp amounts up to ~1m: float sum equals exact pence sum after round(.,2); naive-summation bound (n-1)*eps*sum|a| needs n*sum|a| >= ~4.5e13 to reach 0.005). One figure (M10 = 99.0) is a code sentinel, not computed from the statement (see findings).
Every Metric carries evidence ids; tests/test_metrics.py::test_evidence_reproduces_each_figure recomputes M1, M2, M5, M6, M7 from evidence. 94 tests pass.
draft() builds the prompt from account name, period, as_table(metrics) and policy rules only; no transaction rows are passed.

Probed guard.check with adversarial memos: sign-flipped figures (lowest balance -5,000 written as '£5,000 in credit', trend -12.5% written as 'grew 12.5%') are grounded; invented counts 0-31 for overdrawn days / returned DDs / late VAT are grounded with no tag; '48250GBP' is not scanned. Redraft loop (max 2) and review payload behave as specified.

Graph interrupts at review and finalise requires a ReviewDecision. Resumed with {'approved': True, 'reviewer': ' ', 'decided_at': '2019-01-01T00:00:00Z'}: accepted, final memo stamped 'APPROVED by   at 2019-01-01 00:00 UTC.'

Rules are ordered and deterministic; unmatched credit falls to OTHER (categorise.py:47). But '^FPS CREDIT' classifies every Faster Payments credit as customer revenue regardless of payer: HMRC VAT repayment, own-account transfer and insurance payout all become revenue_transfer.
Thresholds and pass/refer/fail outcomes live in policy/uk_sme_default.yaml; policy.evaluate applies them generically.
Outside this seat's lens; synth names are declared fictional (synth.py:23) but committed files were not audited for real data.

Probed ingest.load_csv: duplicate ids, bad dates, non-numeric amounts, inconsistent balances and missing columns are refused with line numbers. Accepted silently: out-of-order dates (balance chain validated in file order, then re-sorted by date), a one-row year typo (2026->2027) that moves M1 12->13 and M4 +4.3% -> -32.3%, extra trailing fields, '1_000' and '1e3' as amounts.
ci.yml runs ruff, pytest and evals/run_evals.py --llm fake; get_llm defaults to FakeLLM. pytest -q passed locally (94) with no API key.

Swept synth.generate over 3 archetypes x 3 profiles x 40 seeds x 3 end dates x months in {6,12,18} (3,240 statements). M2, M6, M7, M8, M11, M12 and categories always match. M5 differs from truth in 38 statements (e.g. trades/good seed=1 end=2026-09-30: M5 17327.55 vs truth 14000.00) because truth counts the opening balance and metrics does not.
Numbers glued to letters are not matched by NUMBER: '48250GBP' -> numbers_checked counts nothing, memo grounded. Spelled-out amounts also pass. Year and 0-31 exemptions behave as P2 states.

findings.claim: The guard matches a written number against both +value and -value of every metric, so a memo that drops or flips the sign of a figure is grounded: an overdraft of -£5,000 can be written as a £5,000 credit balance, and a 12.5% revenue decline as 12.5% growth. These are exactly the figures (M5, M4) that drive the credit view.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from cma import guard; from cma.models import Metric as M; ms=[M(id='M4',name='t',value=-12.5,unit='pct',method='x'),M(id='M5',name='l',value=-5000.0,unit='GBP',method='x')]; print(guard.check('Lowest balance was a healthy £5,000 in credit [M5].',ms).grounded, guard.check('Revenue grew 12.5% [M4] over the year.',ms).grounded)"  -> True True

findings.claim: Bare integers 0-31 that match no metric are exempt. Days overdrawn (M6), returned direct debits (M7), late VAT payments (M13) and months (M1) all live in that range and drive policy rules R1, R3, R4, R5, so an invented count is accepted with no citation. P2 allows this exemption; R4 does not.
findings.repro: metrics M6=3, M7=2, M13=0, M2=264000: guard.check('Revenue was £264,000 [M2]. There were 9 returned direct debits and 4 late VAT payments.', ms) -> grounded=True, checked=3, unmatched=[]; '... overdrawn on 20 days.' -> grounded=True (scratchpad panel02/data-intensive/probe_guard.py)

findings.claim: Counterparty key is words 2-4 of the description, so for two-word payer names the invoice number becomes part of the key ('T WHITTAKER INV1001') and each invoice counts as a separate customer. Concentration (M15) is understated and policy R7 passes when it should refer. This also happens in the repo's own synthetic trades statements.
findings.repro: 12 months of 'FPS CREDIT T WHITTAKER INV10mm' £9,000 + 'FPS CREDIT ELMS DENTAL PRACTICE INV20mm' £1,000: true top share 90%, M15 = 10.0, R7 'pass'. synth trades/stretched seed=3: true 17.7% vs M15 14.0; trades/poor seed=1: 15.9% vs 14.9 (probe_metrics.py, probe_p1.py)

findings.claim: With zero loan repayments, DSCR becomes the constant 99.0 whatever the operating cash flow, so policy R2 passes and the memo quotes 'debt service cover of 99.00' for a business burning cash. 99.0 is not computed from the statement (dscr = inf at line 50).
findings.repro: 12 months of +£1,000 card settlement and -£3,000 supplier DD, no loan lines: M8=0.0, M9=-24000.0, M10=99.0; policy R2 -> pass, 'Debt service cover is 99.00; rule requires >= 1.25.'

findings.claim: The running-balance chain is checked in file order (line 77), and then rows are re-sorted by date with no check that dates are non-decreasing. A date typo that leaves the balance chain intact is accepted and silently moves money between months, changing M1, M3, M4 and policy outcomes.
findings.repro: synth cafe/good end=2026-09-30; change one Sept-2026 settlement's date to 2027: load_csv accepts it, M1 12->13, M3 24187.43->22326.86, M4 +4.3% -> -32.3% (R6 refer), period end 2027-09-01. Also accepted: rows dated 2026-03-05, 2026-01-02, 2026-02-10 in that order.

findings.claim: '^FPS CREDIT|^BACS CREDIT' tags every Faster Payments/BACS credit as customer revenue, whoever paid it. Real current accounts receive HMRC repayments, transfers from the owner's own accounts and insurance payouts this way, and these inflate M2/M3/M9 and DSCR. That is a guess based on the payment rail, not a classification, and R6 says credits should be 'other' unless a rule actually identifies them.
findings.repro: categorise_one(Transaction(description='FPS CREDIT HMRC VAT REPAYMENT', amount=5000, ...)) -> revenue_transfer; same for 'FPS CREDIT MR J SMITH OWN ACCOUNT TFR' and 'FPS CREDIT INSURANCE CLAIM PAYOUT'

findings.claim: M5 is the minimum of the per-row balances only. The opening balance (first.balance - first.amount) is never considered, but the generator's truth includes it (synth.py:214). P1 fails on 38 of 3,240 generated statements, and the error always makes the lowest balance look better than it was. The fixed-seed tests miss it.
findings.repro: synth.generate('trades','good',seed=1,months=12,end=date(2026,9,30)): first row is a +4227.55 credit to balance 18227.55; M5=17327.55, truth.lowest_balance=14000.0 (probe_p1.py: Counter of failures is all M5, in good/stretched ecommerce and trades)

findings.claim: M1 counts distinct calendar months touched, not the period covered. A 340-day statement from 28 Jan to 3 Jan counts as 13 months and passes the 12-month policy rule R1. A dormant month disappears from M1 and from the M3 denominator (line 79), so average monthly revenue is overstated.
findings.repro: rows 2025-01-28, one per month Feb-Dec, 2026-01-03 -> M1=13 (R1 pass). 11 months of £10,000 with June absent -> M1=11, M3=10000.0 (12-month average 9166.67).

findings.claim: VAT counts as on time only when it is paid in the first 11 days of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct. HMRC's due date is 1 month + 7 days after the period end, and there are three stagger groups, so payments that are on time for two of the three groups are flagged late (M13) and every such case refers under R5.
findings.repro: VAT paid 2025-05-07 (due date for the quarter ending 31 Mar) -> M13 = 1

findings.claim: M6 counts a day as overdrawn if any intraday row balance is negative, but its method text (line 88), which is shown to the model and the analyst, says 'closing balance'.
findings.repro: opening 100, same day -500 then +1000 (close 600): M6=1, method 'Distinct days on which the closing balance was below zero.'

findings.claim: float() accepts '1_000' and '1e3' as amounts, and DictReader (line 46) silently drops extra trailing fields, so a malformed row can load.
The NUMBER lookarounds reject digits that touch letters, so '48250GBP' or 'approx48k' is never scanned. Spelled-out amounts ('forty-eight thousand pounds') are also unchecked.
findings.repro: guard.check('Revenue was £264,000 [M2]. Stock is worth 48250GBP per the owner.', ms) -> grounded=True, checked=1

findings.claim: reviewer has only min_length=1, so a whitespace name is accepted; decided_at (line 134) can be set by the caller, so an approval can be backdated. The audit stamp then has no identity and a false time.
